paper.title: Large Language Model Agents Are Not Always Faithful Self-Evolvers
paper.central_claim: Across four self-evolving agent frameworks, 13 backbones and nine environments, agents consistently depend on raw experience but often disregard or misinterpret condensed experience, even when it is the only experience; the gap persists across multi-agent settings and scale and is traced to semantic limits of condensed content, internal processing biases and task regimes where priors suffice.
paper.scope_note: In scope as a B-class audit of retained non-weight memory in existing frameworks.

provenance.notes: Opus aggregate seat via the configured claude-kimi type fable; no route probing. actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref are null because the subagent runtime exposes no verifiable provider receipt to this worker.

evidence.quote: Despite their central role, prior work has focused mainly on how such experiences are stored or represented, leaving it unclear whether agents actually and faithfully leverage them to improve performance.

evidence.quote: While these methods offer promising pathways for autonomous improvement, little attention has been paid to whether agents faithfully rely on the retrieved experiences—a gap our work aims to address.

evidence.quote: In all frameworks, the LLM backbone remains frozen, and behavioral adaptation arises solely from the accumulation, retrieval, and exploitation of external experiences.

evidence.quote: A surprising observation from our interventions is that agents sometimes perform better when condensed experience is perturbed or removed. This suggests that condensed summaries may be uninformative or misaligned.
evidence.support_explanation: Author's cause #1, supported by post-hoc failure categories (Table 1) without matched denominators.

evidence.quote: In summary, these trends suggest that even when presented with semantically rich (or intervened) summaries, condensed experience struggles to influence downstream behavior due to structural biases in the model’s attention flow.
evidence.support_explanation: Author's cause #2, supported only by attribution scores (no intervention on attention/position).

evidence.quote: This suggests that the utility of experience is highly task-dependent: when a task can be handled with the agent’s innate knowledge, the retrieved experience contributes little and thus fails to exert meaningful causal influence.
evidence.support_explanation: Author's cause #3 and a stated task boundary.

evidence.quote: Rather than abstract summaries or generic advice, effective condensed experience should be contextualized, task-relevant, and cognitively actionable.
evidence.support_explanation: Design takeaways are untested suggestions; no mitigation, no improved condensation or gating is implemented or evaluated.

evidence.quote: Perturbing raw trajectories, particularly through Empty or Irrelevant replacements, produces similarly severe declines.
evidence.support_explanation: Author claim; Fig. 2 HotpotQA shows Irrelevant 45 vs 47 (no decline) and Shuffle 46; ALFWorld/WebShop Shuffle only -2 to -6, so reliance is on content presence/relevance rather than ordering.

evidence.quote: However, in knowledge-grounded tasks such as FEVER, the impact of raw experience perturbation is less pronounced.
evidence.support_explanation: Author acknowledgement of a regime where the asymmetry does not hold (FEVER).

evidence.quote: We observe that in certain knowledge-intensive tasks such as GPQA-Diamond and MMLU-Pro Eng., the agent exhibits comparable sensitivity to both raw and condensed experience.
evidence.support_explanation: Author acknowledgement of exceptions on GPQA-Diamond / MMLU-Pro (DC-RS).

evidence.quote: we set the decoding temperature to 0.7 and adopt greedy decoding as the decoding strategy.

evidence.quote: Task outcomes are labeled as success or failure using LLM-as-a-judge

evidence.quote: Our experiments span 10 LLMs, including closed-source models:

evidence.quote: At evaluation time, ExpeL retrieves the top-k most similar successful trajectories and uses them as in-context demonstrations.
evidence.support_explanation: In ExpeL raw trajectories are few-shot demonstrations that also fix the action/output format; ALFWorld/WebShop collapse to ~0% when they are removed or emptied (Fig. 2/8). Raw and condensed memory therefore differ in functional role, not only abstraction level.

evidence.quote: After each task, the agent examines the produced output and selectively updates the memory by preserving entries that appear useful, while modifying or removing ineffective ones.
evidence.support_explanation: Studied framework's own retention rule (self-judged); the paper neither manipulates nor evaluates this rule.

evidence.quote: Following each task completion, the agent assesses its own performance and selectively incorporates newly acquired experiences into this memory repository.
evidence.support_explanation: Studied framework's own retention rule (self-assessed); not manipulated by the paper.

evidence.quote: we reveal a persistent and systematic gap: agents reliably depend on raw trajectories but frequently overlook or misinterpret condensed summaries.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline conclusion stated without any limitations section; wording 'reliably'/'persistent' is stronger than several cells in Figs. 8-14.

evidence.quote: In contrast, we study faithfulness in self-evolving agentic settings, where experience is both dynamic and multifaceted, revealing emerging phenomena beyond static prompt usage.
evidence.support_explanation: Lineage: ICL-demonstration faithfulness (Min et al. 2022; Ye & Durrett 2022; Shi et al. 2024) and CoT faithfulness (Lanham et al. 2023; Turpin et al. 2023) are the named ancestors; these sources are cited but not pinned locally.

evidence.quote: Faithfulness is determined by whether the agent’s behavior causally changes in response to the perturbed input.
evidence.support_explanation: Fig. 1 schematic: perturbation types (Shuffle, Corrupt, Irrelevant) and the decision 'behavior change vs behavior maintenance'; the measured behaviour in all experiments is the aggregate success rate, no action-level divergence is reported.

evidence.quote: We strictly follow the official configuration of each agent framework.
evidence.support_explanation: All intervention arms within a framework share the official configuration (steps, retrieval k, decoding), hence equal interaction budget per arm; no compute/token/dollar cost is stated.

evidence.quote: Representative cases are shown in Table 4, Table 5, and Table 6, respectively.
evidence.support_explanation: Three anecdotal with/without-memory traces (WebArena Shopping/CMS) illustrate failure categories; no counts of how many failures fall in each beyond Table 1 percentages, and the Table 6 and Table 4 evaluator verdicts are LLM-written.

claims.text: With both raw and condensed memory present (ExpeL, Dynamic Cheatsheet), raw perturbations change behaviour strongly and condensed perturbations barely.
claims.setting: ExpeL GPT-4o on HotpotQA/ALFWorld/WebShop (n=100/134/100); DC-RS GPT-4o on AIME/Game24/GPQA/MMLU-Pro; replicated for ExpeL on Qwen3-235B and Claude-Sonnet-4.6
claims.baseline_control: Unperturbed framework, w/o raw, w/o cond, Empty, Filler; official configs; single run
claims.selection_vs_test: No selection or tuning split; single evaluation set; a-priori interventions
claims.result_denominator: ALFWorld GPT-4o: w/o raw 0 vs 75, Irrelevant 33.6, Shuffle 69.4; condensed 72.4-76.9. WebShop 0/0 vs 30. HotpotQA raw w/o 24 vs 47 but Irrelevant 45, Shuffle 46. Game24 raw 34-57 vs 99; condensed 84-96. AIME +-3.3 steps = 1 problem. Denominators 100/134/30, no CI.
counterevidence: E031 (Claude HotpotQA raw +3 to +5, condensed Empty -6; ALFWorld cond Empty -9)
E030 (Qwen3-235B HotpotQA raw 42-49 vs 46; WebShop condensed Empty -13)
claims.allowed_conclusion: On ALFWorld/WebShop (ExpeL) and Game of 24 (DC-RS) the success rate collapses when raw demonstrations are removed or replaced, whereas content perturbations of condensed memory move it by about 5 points or less; this is not shown to be a faithfulness difference rather than a functional-role or perturbation-strength difference, and does not hold on HotpotQA with several backbones.

claims.text: The condensed-memory insensitivity persists when condensed experience is the only memory (ReasoningBank).
claims.setting: ReasoningBank WebArena Shopping/CMS/Reddit/Map; Gemini-2.5-Flash (main), Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-32B, Gemini-3-Pro
claims.baseline_control: w/o condensed and ReasoningBank baseline; Empty/Corrupt/Irrelevant/Filler; single runs, temperature 0.7
claims.selection_vs_test: Online stream, memory built on the same evaluated tasks; no held-out split described
claims.result_denominator: Gemini-2.5-Flash: RB 59.4/60.4/49.1/60.6 vs w/o 56.7/47.8/47.8/54.1; perturbations -9 to +6 (Reddit panel appears duplicated from CMS). Qwen3-32B: memory adds 0.5-3.9 points; Corrupt/Irrelevant/Filler up to -8.5/-11 in CMS/Reddit/Map. Qwen3-14B: perturbations +5..+11 in CMS. Gemini-3-Pro: Shopping/CMS all perturbations -3..-8. n=187/182/106/109.
counterevidence: E038 contradicted by Empty < w/o in Shopping/Map
claims.allowed_conclusion: Condensed-only memory yields mixed, backbone- and domain-dependent sensitivity to content perturbation; 'negligible' holds for part of the cells and is contradicted in others; absence of benefit over w/o in several cells limits what insensitivity can show.
claims.opus_allowed_conclusion: Reddit panel of Fig. 4 is a duplicate of CMS (opus:O03) and is excluded; the condensed-only conclusion rests on Shopping/CMS/Map and the Qwen3-14B/32B and Gemini-3-Pro replications, which are mixed.

claims.text: The raw/condensed asymmetry persists in multi-agent G-Memory.
claims.setting: G-Memory on FEVER and ALFWorld with GPT-4o-mini, Qwen3-235B-A22B, GPT-5.2
claims.baseline_control: Unperturbed G-Memory; Ref-raw, Exe-raw and condensed interventions; single runs

claims.allowed_conclusion: On ALFWorld, reference-raw perturbations reduce success substantially for three backbones and condensed ones do not; self-generated raw memory is less consistently relied upon; FEVER shows no asymmetry.

claims.text: The gap persists across model scale; scaling does not resolve it.

claims.baseline_control: ExpeL baseline per model; raw 3 and condensed 4 interventions; no w/o bars

claims.text: Cause 1: condensed content is semantically limited and can mislead (distraction, wrong priors, premature inference).
claims.setting: ReasoningBank WebArena, cases that succeed without but fail with condensed memory
claims.baseline_control: None beyond with/without; no control for cases where condensed memory helped
claims.result_denominator: Percentages only (Qwen3-32B/14B distraction 60-87%, Gemini-2.5-Flash spread); cell counts implied ~20-40 and unreported

claims.text: Cause 2: internal processing bias (local-context dominance) suppresses condensed experience.
claims.result_denominator: Normalized IG: condensed ~0.1, raw ~0.2-0.25, current trajectory 0.4-0.55 (Qwen3-32B); Empty raises condensed attribution to ~0.3-0.46 in early layers
claims.allowed_conclusion: Gradient-based attribution assigns low weight to the condensed block in these models; this is correlational and sensitive to segment length/format, not a demonstrated cause.

claims.text: Cause 3: in knowledge-intensive tasks where pretrained priors suffice, neither raw nor condensed experience matters.
claims.setting: ExpeL on 2WikiMultiHopQA and Musique (n=100, EM); Qwen3-32B and Qwen3-14B; plus FEVER/GPQA/MMLU-Pro observations
claims.baseline_control: Unperturbed ExpeL; raw 3 and condensed 4 interventions
claims.result_denominator: Qwen3-32B: all interventions within about 5 points (62/48 baseline); Qwen3-14B: 55-60 vs 60 and 34-44 vs 37.
counterevidence: No test that priors cause it (e.g. closed-book accuracy, contamination check)
claims.allowed_conclusion: On these tasks and models perturbations of either memory type change EM by only a few points, consistent with limited marginal use of experience; the prior-knowledge explanation is plausible but untested.

assessment.evidence_level_note: No EVIDENCE.md level: the paper is a diagnostic of how existing frameworks use retained memory, with no claim that retained experience improves later held-out tasks or the improver.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In single-run configurations, removing or replacing retrieved raw trajectories usually lowers success far more than perturbing condensed insights in ExpeL (ALFWorld, WebShop), Dynamic Cheatsheet (Game of 24) and G-Memory (ALFWorld); on knowledge-heavy tasks and AIME neither matters measurably. Author-reported; the Fig. 4 Reddit panel is a duplicate and AIME is a 30-problem set.

G.reason: Both seats 3; verified. Concrete evaluation gap: memory frameworks report gains from retained condensed experience without testing whether its content is used; ICL/CoT faithfulness lineage is named. 'First systematic' unsupported by a search and memory-ablation neighbours are not compared, so not 4.

M.reason: Both seats 3; verified. Empty vs w/o vs Filler separate presence/format from content; condensed-only ReasoningBank removes overshadowing; scale and task-regime checks give distinguishable predictions. Not 4: perturbation strength is unmatched between raw and condensed, 'Corrupt' as shown is token masking rather than the promised inversion, and success rate is the only behaviour proxy. Raw 'Irrelevant' does preserve format (opus:O05), so the design partly answers the format confound.

X.reason: Both seats 3; verified. Intervention types with examples, official framework configs, benchmark sizes and backbones are given. Not 4: online injection timing unstated, Fig. 6 benchmark unnamed, IG description inconsistent, ReasoningBank decoding contradictory (opus:O08), 10 vs 13 backbones (opus:O06/O07), no limitations section.

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 2; verified and reasoning extended. Environment success/EM are standard, but the construct (faithfulness = behaviour change) is measured only as change in aggregate success; WebArena/ReasoningBank uses an LLM judge; Table 1 has no counts. Opus confirms two data-integrity defects that only son55 had flagged: the Fig. 4 Reddit panel duplicates the CMS bars and is unattainable for n=106 (opus:O03/O04), and AIME is reported as 133 problems while the bars are 30-problem multiples (opus:O01/O02). Both are confined to single panels and do not lower the item below 2.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; verified. Real content manipulations across four frameworks give a raw-vs-condensed sensitivity gap in several cells; alternatives remain: raw demonstrations also fix format (partly answered by format-preserving 'Irrelevant', opus:O05, which may itself mislead), unmatched perturbation strength, weak 'Corrupt', no misleading-content probe, floor effects where memory adds ~0, and causes 2–3 rest on attribution only.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 2; verified.
